deep.reconstruction:
This page contains no mathematics. It is a handwritten description of a social dance, the 'Berliner Contra', a quadrille-type contredanse for four couples. It is numbered '4.' at the top left and continues the previous page, which describes the 'Pariser Contra'.

Structure of the page:
(a) Stellung (set-up): a diagram of a square of dancers, with the key 'o = Damen, + = Herren' (o = ladies, + = gentlemen). Four couples stand on the four sides of the square.
(b) 1te Tour: the whole column advances and retires, apparently 'with 2 x 5' (steps). The 1st couple goes forward and back, across, right, left, back to place. Then a figure (read as 'Balabar[?]') and a 'kleine Runde' (small circle). Couples 2, 3 and 4 repeat it.
(c) 2te Tour: the 1st couple swings out the opposite lady, takes its own lady with the left hand, and dances 3 steps of a back-to-back figure, probably 'dos-à-dos' spelled phonetically. Chassez to the opposite side, across. Then everyone does the dos-à-dos and a small circle.
(d) 3te Tour: swinging out in a circle. The 1st couple goes forward, back, across, right, left, to place. Swinging out in a circle again. Couples 2, 3 and 4 repeat it.
(e) 4te Tour: the 1st couple goes forward, back, across, right, left, to place. Then forward with the ladies, 'Belle deux[?]', contra chassez, turn to the right back to place.
(f) 5te Tour: couples 1 and 2 go forward with the ladies, contra chassez, turn right back to place. The 1st couple swings out the opposite lady, takes its own with the left hand, and ends with a Promenade. The page closes with a flourish.

There are no derivations, formulas, computations or mathematical problems to reconstruct. The page belongs to the 'Varia' bundle as personal or social material: dance notes, plausibly from Riemann's student years or from a family member. The hand matches the previous page.
errors: No mathematical content, so there are no mathematical errors to report.

The dance terminology mixes French terms written phonetically or idiosyncratically: 'Dosheid'/'Dos...' is probably 'dos-à-dos', and 'Belle deux' perhaps 'balancez' or a corrupted French term. These are orthographic quirks, not errors of substance.

results.what: Written instructions (figures/tours) for the 'Berliner Contra', a square contredanse/quadrille for four couples
results.usually_credited_to: Traditional 19th-century social dance; no individual author

deep.surprise_reason: The page is a dance description with no mathematical content. Its presence among Riemann's miscellaneous papers is a minor biographical curiosity, not a mathematical finding.

checkable.asserts: Trivial consistency of the set-up diagram: four couples (one per side of the square), i.e. 8 dancers. There is no genuine mathematical claim on the page.

transcription_corrections: Tour labels read '1te Tour', '2te Tour', ... '5te Tour' in the image (ordinal 'te'), not '1r Tour' etc.
1te Tour: 'mit zweimal 3' is more likely 'mit 2mal 5' (cf. '2mal 5' on the previous page).
'wechselweise [?]' is uncertain; the word after 'zurück –' may instead be 'mehrmal' or similar. The reading remains doubtful.
2te Tour: 'die eigene und u. tanzt' is probably 'die eigene um u. tanzt' (takes his own lady round). The duplicated 'und u.' is a transcription artefact.
'Dosheid' is probably a phonetic or idiosyncratic spelling of 'dos-à-dos'.
'Belle deux [?]' and 'Balabar [?]' are uncertain French dance terms; the previous page has the same 'belle deux' reading, so it is at least consistent.
